answer: Only crystals catalogued inside the ice cave earn a seat, because the tally book holds the weight and shape of every crystal the keeper has seen. A quill crystal bought at market fails the book: at the horizon of the cave the crystal must carry the cave's own frost, and market ice shows no frost at all. Forging a tally means bribing the keeper, faking a winter of cataloguing and paying 11,300, while the vertex entry in the tally book is read at every sale, so a crystal whose cave was never entered is turned away.
